data.title: Model Context Protocol
data.tagline: A connection protocol AI applications use to discover and call external tools, data, and prompts
data.learningOutcome: You can identify the application, server, and tool in one connection while keeping permission checks in place.
data.description: When a user asks who owns issue #1024, the application discovers get_ticket from an MCP server and sends the lookup. The issue tracker checks read permission and returns Alex. MCP standardizes the connection; it does not replace the real system or its authorization.

learning.assumes: You know an AI agent can use tools to read files or call an outside service.
learning.outcome: You can identify the application, server, and tool in one connection while keeping permission checks in place.

explanation.title: Configuring and exposing tools
explanation.text: Add server command configs in your AI tool settings. The MCP server announces which tools (like get_ticket) it exposes and what arguments they expect.

explanation.title: The AI application requests the call
explanation.text: The model proposes get_ticket({ id: 1024 }), and the MCP client sends it to the issue service.

explanation.title: The issue tracker returns the real record
explanation.text: It checks the test account's read access and returns the owner. MCP does not store the issue or decide permission.

data.boundary: MCP is not the get_ticket tool or the issue service itself. It standardizes discovery and calls; the application and issue tracker still own authorization, real records, and high-risk confirmation.

lessonPractice.title: A user asks who owns issue #1024. After the application discovers get_ticket through MCP, what should happen next?

options.label: The app requests get_ticket({ id: 1024 }), and the issue tracker checks the current account before returning the real record
options.feedback: Correct. MCP handles tool discovery and the call; the issue tracker still handles authorization and real data.

options.label: Because it uses MCP, the application can skip the issue tracker's account check
options.feedback: A connection protocol is not authorization. The issue tracker still decides whether this account may read #1024.

options.label: Let the model guess an owner from the issue number without calling the tool
options.feedback: The owner must come from the real record returned by the tool, not a model guess.

data.agentPrompt: Use MCP to retrieve issue #1024 with a read-only test account. First confirm that the issue service exposes get_ticket, then show the actual arguments, account permission, and tool result. Do not expose close or delete actions.
